title: 1951 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In the equation \[ \frac{x(x-1)-(m+1)}{(x-1)(m-1)}=\frac{x}{m}, \] the roots are equal when:

solutions.text:
Clearing denominators and simplifying yields \[ x^2-x-m(m+1)=0. \] Equal roots require \[ \begin{aligned} 1+4m(m+1) &=(2m+1)^2\\ &=0, \end{aligned} \] hence \(m=-\frac12.\) This value does not violate the original denominators.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Clear denominators and collect the resulting quadratic in \(x\)
The equation reduces to \(x^2-x-m(m+1)=0\); equal roots require zero discriminant
